title: A Novel Method for Localizing Reporter Fluorescent Beads Near the Cell Culture Surface for Traction Force Microscopy
protocol: Clean glass cover slips (#1.0, 12 mm diam.) with soap and water.
Rinse clean glass cover slips with ethanol.
Place cleaned glass cover slips on a grated surface such that they are not touching.
Coat the entire surface of the cover slips with Poly-D-Lysine (0.1 mg/ml) for 1 hr.

Perform a 1:10,000 dilution of the colloid solution of 0.1 μm diameter red fluorescent microspheres with deionized water to obtain a particle density of approximately 1 microsphere per 20 μm² on the gel surface.
Place the diluted solution in an ultrasonic water bath for 30 min.
After 1 hr, use tweezers to carefully lift each cover slip and blow dry with air.
Return the dried cover slips to the grated surface.
Remove the diluted colloid solution from the ultrasonic bath and pipette 150 μl onto each cover slip.
Leave the cover slips coated with the colloid solution for 10 min.
Use tweezers to carefully lift each cover slip and blow dry with air again.
Return the dried cover slips to the grated surface and store in the dark until ready to use.
Lay out the desired number of glass bottom Petri dishes (35 mm dish with 14 mm micro-well) on a flat surface in a chemical fume hood.
Cover the glass portion of each Petri dish micro-well with 97% 3-aminopropyl-trimethoxysilane (3-APTES) for 7 min for chemical activation.
Fill the Petri dish with DI water and dispose into waste container.
Repeat step 2.4 three times for each dish, and then shake the Petri dish to remove extra water.
Place the Petri dishes on a hot plate until the glass portion is dry.
In a chemical fume hood, make a solution of 0.5% glutaraldehyde.
Cover the glass portion of each Petri dish well with the glutaraldehyde solution for 30 min.
Fill the Petri dish with DI water and dispose into waste container to rinse and remove the glutaraldehyde.
Repeat step 2.4 three times for each dish, and then shake the Petri dish to remove extra water.
Place the Petri dishes on a hot plate until the glass portion is dry.
Move functionalized glass slides into the chemical fume hood for easy access.
Mix 40% bisacrylamide, 2% acrylamide, and acrylic acid in a 15 ml centrifuge tube according to Table 1 concentrations.
Add 100 mM HEPES, 10% ammonium persulfate, and TEMED to the mixture as per Table 1 quantities.
Pipette 15 μl of gel solution onto the center of the glass portion of petri dishes immediately after mixing.
Pick up a functionalized glass cover slip with tweezers.
Flip the glass cover slip over so that the fluorescent beads are on the side contacting the gel solution.
Lay the cover slip gently on top of the liquid PA gel such that the functionalized side contacts the gel.
Flip all Petri dishes over to assist with avoiding gravity effects on fluorescent nanoparticles polymerizing into lower levels of the PA gel.
Wait for at least 35 min or until the stock solution of PA gel has visibly polymerized.
Flip the Petri dishes back over and fill them with PBS to assist with removing the cover slip.
Use tweezers to scrape the circumference of the cover slip, making contact with the glass portion of the Petri dish.
Perform several cycles until the cover slip is dislodged.
Remove the cover slip and dispose in a proper sharps waste container.
Cover the PA gels completely with PBS after removing all cover slips.
Place the Petri dish lid on each dish and store at 4 °C.
Soak solution (137 mM NaCl, 5% (v/v) glycerol).
Pipette soak solution onto each gel such that the gel is completely submerged.
Incubate at room temperature for at least 1 hr.
Warm EDC and NHS to room temperature.
Mix 10x solutions of EDC (150 mM, 19 mg/ml in DI water) and NHS (250 mM, 29 mg/ml in DI water).
Mix 1 part 10x EDC with 1 part 10x NHS.
Add 3 parts DI water and 5 parts 2x conjugation buffer to the mixture.
Use a vacuum pump in a biological hood to remove the soak solution from the gel surface.
Ensure all fluid is removed from the gel surface.
Add enough NHS/EDC solution to cover the gel surface and fill the glass-bottom well of the Petri dish (150–250 μl).
Incubate at room temperature for 30 min in the dark.
Thaw fibronectin at room temperature.
Mix sterile DI water with thawed fibronectin to create a 50 μg/ml solution.
Use a vacuum pump in a biological hood to remove the NHS/EDC solution from the gel surface.
Ensure all fluid is removed from the gel surface.
Add 150 μl of fibronectin solution to each gel.
Incubate at room temperature for 35 min to allow for attachment of fibronectin.
After 35 min, add PBS to each Petri dish.
Store at 4 °C for up to 2 weeks.
Warm cell media, PBS, and trypsin to 37 °C in a water bath.
Rinse gels 5 times with sterile PBS, aspirating the PBS between rinses, and leave covered in the hood.
Add 1 ml trypsin per 25 cm² to flask containing cells.
After cells are lifted from flask, dilute the trypsin with cell media.
Count the cells.
Based on gel surface area, determine the number of cells required for a final density of 3,000 cells/cm².
Dilute or concentrate suspension such that 150 μl of the cell-media mixture contains this number of cells.
Aliquot 150 μl of cell suspension onto each gel.
Place the Petri dishes containing cells in an incubator for 30 min.
Remove the Petri dishes from the incubator and fill them with approximately 2 ml of media.
Return the Petri dishes to the incubator until image acquisition is ready.
Prepare the microscope by inserting a 40x water immersion objective.
Insert the Differential Interference Contrast (DIC) prism into the microscope setup.
Select the mCherry or equivalent fluorescent filter for imaging.
Turn on the environmental chamber for controlled conditions during imaging.
Remove one Petri dish from the incubator and place it gently on the microscope stage.
Remove the lid of the Petri dish for DIC imaging.
Locate a single cell using the microscope and capture a still image in DIC mode.
Switch the imaging mode to fluorescence without moving the microscope stage.
Focus on the fluorescent microspheres and record an image of them.
Pipette out the cell media from the Petri dish and add 0.05% trypsin-EDTA solution.
Capture images of the microspheres under the detached cells.
Use particle image velocimetry (PIV) analysis in ImageJ to compute the displacement field due to cellular forces.
